title: HIIT Workouts in NZ Gyms
meta_desc: Discover the best HIIT workouts in NZ gyms, comparing F45, Orangetheory, and DIY options, including cost and effectiveness, with NZ gym chains like City Fitness, Les Mills, and Jetts
intro: High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) has become a staple in many NZ gyms, with boutique studios like F45 and Orangetheory offering specialised classes. However, you can also create your own HIIT workouts at a standard gym. In this guide, we'll compare the costs and effectiveness of these options, helping you decide what's best for your fitness journey. With the help of Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme, you can get 40-70% off your gym membership, making it more affordable to try out different HIIT options.

sections.heading: What is HIIT and its Benefits?
sections.body: HIIT involves short bursts of intense exercise followed by brief periods of rest. This type of training has been shown to improve cardiovascular health, increase calorie burn, and enhance muscular endurance. Many NZ gyms, including City Fitness and Les Mills, offer HIIT-based group fitness classes, which can be a great way to get started with this type of training. Additionally, you can use the equipment and facilities at gyms like Jetts and Anytime Fitness to create your own HIIT workouts.

sections.heading: Boutique HIIT Studios: F45 and Orangetheory
sections.body: F45 and Orangetheory are two popular boutique HIIT studios in NZ, offering high-energy classes with experienced trainers. These studios typically offer a more structured and motivating environment, with classes designed to push you to your limits. However, they often come with a higher price tag, with prices ranging from $20 to $30 per class. In comparison, a standard gym membership can cost between $10 to $20 per week, depending on the gym chain and contract length.

sections.heading: DIY HIIT Workouts at a Standard Gym
sections.body: Creating your own HIIT workout at a standard gym can be a cost-effective and flexible option. You can use the gym's equipment, such as treadmills, stationary bikes, and free weights, to design your own HIIT routine. Many gyms, including City Fitness and Jetts, offer a variety of equipment and facilities that can be used for HIIT training. Additionally, you can use online resources and apps to find HIIT workouts and follow along.
list: Use gym equipment like treadmills and stationary bikes
Design your own HIIT routine using online resources
Follow along with HIIT workouts on apps like Nike Training Club

sections.heading: Cost Comparison and Effectiveness
sections.body: When comparing the costs of boutique HIIT studios and DIY HIIT workouts at a standard gym, it's clear that the latter is a more affordable option. With a standard gym membership, you can create your own HIIT workouts and use the gym's equipment and facilities without the high cost of boutique studios. However, the effectiveness of your workout depends on your motivation and dedication. If you prefer a more structured and motivating environment, a boutique studio might be the better option for you.

sections.heading: Getting Started with HIIT in NZ Gyms
sections.body: To get started with HIIT in NZ gyms, consider the following tips: start with shorter intervals and gradually increase the duration and intensity, find a workout buddy or join a group fitness class to stay motivated, and mix up your routine to avoid plateaus.
